description_full: Healthcare Realty Trust Incorporated is a real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns and operates medical outpatient buildings primarily located around market-leading hospital campuses. The Company selectively grows its portfolio through property acquisition and development. As of September 30, 2025, the Company was invested in 579 real estate properties in 28 states totaling 33.6 million square feet and had an enterprise value of approximately 11.1 billion dollars, defined as equity market capitalization plus the principal amount of debt less cash. Healthcare Realty Trust Incorporated was incorporated in 1992 and is based in Nashville, United States.

Each employee generates $236K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $42K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: Healthcare Realty Trust Incorpo is a mid-cap real estate business with a $6.7B market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 2% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The business throws off $127M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 6.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
